evidence: app/package.json:7 — pins nuxt 4.6.3, the current stable release (GitHub releases, Oct 27 2026), not a canary/RC
app/nuxt.config.ts:2-18 — config uses only compatibilityDate, css, runtimeConfig.public, app.head; no experimental/unstable flags or future flags
app/app/pages/index.vue:17 — plain await useAsyncData(key, fn), the long-stable data-fetching API

reach.rationale: Only long-stable APIs. Zero experimental markers, no Nuxt 4.6 preview features (nuxt/server, Vapor, vite-server, appSecret sessions) despite the app using the newest stable release that ships them.

evidence: app/app/utils/poke.ts:1-200 — all data access funnelled through one hand-rolled module (fetchApi/fetchRecord) built on stable $fetch
app/app/plugins/api-base.ts:1-4 — the only stateful touch of Nuxt internals, a 4-line plugin using stable defineNuxtPlugin/$config
app/app/components/NotFound.vue:6 — the closest thing to an internal: event.node.res.statusCode = 404, confined to a single shared component and repeated in pages/pokemon/[name].vue:172-173
containment.rationale: Nothing experimental to contain. The single forward-sensitive pattern (h3 v1 event.node.res) sits behind one shared NotFound component plus one line in the Pokémon page.

evidence: app/app/pages/moves/[name].vue:5 — stable useAsyncData for every page's data needs; spec needs nothing newer
app/app/pages/[...path].vue:1-3 — catch-all 404 route via stable file-based routing rather than any new routing API
app/nuxt.config.ts:3 — compatibilityDate '2025-01-01' opted in deliberately rather than reaching for future flags
justification.rationale: No experimental APIs are used at all, and none were needed: every spec requirement is met with APIs that have been stable across Nuxt 3/4.

findings.issue: Sets the 404 status by mutating h3 v1 internals (event.node.res.statusCode). This is stable today, but Nuxt 4.6 introduced the nuxt/server portable RequestEvent surface specifically to smooth the path to h3 v2 / Nitro v3 in Nuxt 5.
findings.suggestion: Prefer the stable, future-proof alternative: `throw createError({ statusCode: 404 })` in a page/middleware, or setResponseStatus from nuxt/server (h3's own API) — behavior identical, less coupled to h3 v1 internals. Mirror the same change in app/app/pages/pokemon/[name].vue:172-173 and the other pages repeating this pattern (moves/[name].vue:36, abilities/[name].vue:31, types/[name].vue:45).

summary: This app is maximally conservative on the experimentalness axis: it pins the current stable Nuxt 4.6.3 and uses exclusively long-stable APIs (useAsyncData, useHead, useRequestEvent, defineNuxtPlugin, NuxtLink, $fetch), ignoring every preview surface Nuxt 4.6 shipped. The only forward-compat wrinkle is direct mutation of h3 v1's event.node.res for 404 statuses in a handful of pages, which stable alternatives exist for. Risk of framework churn breaking this code is minimal.
